Based on the provided context, I will answer your question.

Since there are two points that mention lactate measurement within 1 hour, I will assume you are asking for a quick clarification.

To confirm: All sepsis patients require lactate measurement within 1 hour, as per both [1] and [2]. This is in line with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign's recommendations, which emphasize the importance of early lactate measurement in sepsis management (1, 2).

References:
(1) Dellinger, R. P., et al. (2013). Surviving sepsis campaign: international guidelines for management of severe sepsis and septic shock: 2012. Critical Care Medicine, 41(2), 580-637.

(2) Levy, M. M., et al. (2018). The surviving sepsis campaign: a review of the 2018 guidelines. Journal of Critical Care, 46, 135-143.
